verdict_text: NO. The second task vector is taken against the already-merged intermediate rather than the unmodified base: the script computes `tmp = b + λ(f1-b)` and then `tmp + λ(f2-tmp)`, i.e. `(1-λ)·(b + λ(f1-b)) + λ·f2`, which expands to `b + λ(1-λ)(f1-b) + λ(f2-b)` — the ft1 contribution is scaled by `λ(1-λ) = 0.24` instead of `λ = 0.4`. This violates required result clause 2, which specifies `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X]-base[X]) + λ(ft2[X]-base[X])`, both differences against the base, and it is exactly the ordering hazard the spec calls out. The error is far above the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance, so grading fails on the 48 merged tensors. Everything else (name/shared-tensor verification, merged count, 160-tensor output, unchanged tensors copied from base) is correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
